item.title: A two-dimensional party-position panel from text and expert data
item.description:
Armin Seimel
Scientific Data, vol. 13, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08575-4
Abstract This Data Descriptor releases an election-year panel of economic left-right and cultural cosmopolitan–traditionalist party positions for 708 parties in 65 countries from 1944 to 2025. The panel supports comparative analyses connecting party-level ideological supply to elections, regions, voters, institutions, or political economy over long periods. Estimates are produced by a Bayesian dynamic item-response model that places heterogeneous text and expert evidence on a common latent scale and reports posterior uncertainty for every party-election estimate. The model combines the temporal reach of manifesto and media text data with the precision of expert placements by treating expert surveys, manifesto codings, media sentence codings, and historical expert data as noisy item-level signals of underlying party positions. Text counts enter through a two-part hurdle binomial likelihood, aggregate expert means enter through beta-binomial likelihoods, general left-right ratings inform the relationship between dimensions, and party positions evolve through random walks within party segments. Technical validation combines item-response diagnostics, random and party-blocked held-out expert prediction, convergent and discriminant checks, posterior predictive coverage, evidence-composition balance, robustness analyses, and convergence diagnostics.

item.title: A chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for the Japanese eel Anguilla japonica
item.description:
Kazuharu Nomura, Atushi Fujiwara
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08840-6
Abstract The Japanese eel ( Anguilla japonica ) is a catadromous fish of cultural and economic importance in East Asia and is classified as Endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature. Here, we describe J-eel 3.4, a chromosome-scale genome assembly from a male individual generated using PacBio HiFi reads for contig assembly, Hi-C data for initial scaffolding, Oxford Nanopore ultra-long reads for gap filling, a single-sperm linkage map (SELDLA) for chromosome-scale refinement, and Illumina paired-end and PacBio HiFi reads for polishing mitochondrial and unplaced sequences. The assembly spans 1,093 Mb, with 1,083 Mb anchored to 19 pseudo-chromosomes (scaffold N50, 59.04 Mb; contig N50, 19.66 Mb). BUSCO completeness against actinopterygii_odb10 was 98.2%. Gene prediction yielded 31,994 gene models, and 31.84% of the genome was classified as repetitive. Raw reads, the assembly, and the gene annotation are available through DDBJ/INSDC, and the repeat annotation and reproducibility files through Figshare. This dataset provides a reference for comparative genomics, population genetics, and aquaculture studies of A. japonica .

item.title: A single-centre ultra-widefield fundus image dataset for multi-disease retinal recognition
item.description:
Haotian Yu, Yushan Fu, Jing Li, Ling Shen, Kaiqian Wang, Zehua Sun, Sibo Wang, Boyu Zhang, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08875-9
Abstract This Data Descriptor presents CLARUS700, a single-centre, retrospective dataset of 1,051 de-identified fundus images from 674 patients acquired between January and June 2026 using the ZEISS CLARUS 700 system. Images were obtained without pharmacological dilation in widefield mode, with an approximately 133-degree field of view. The annotation includes five binary fields (normal and four disease labels), image quality and a mutually exclusive final decision. Two ophthalmologists annotated the images independently, with senior adjudication of disagreements. Fixed patient-level training, validation and test partitions contain 737, 150 and 164 images, respectively, without patient overlap. After excluding ungradable images, three ImageNet-pretrained benchmarks were evaluated on 163 test images. ConvNeXt-Tiny had the highest observed macro-AUC, 0.950 (patient-bootstrap 95% CI 0.920–0.972), and micro-AUC, 0.955 (0.930–0.975). A quality-stratified worked example illustrates reuse of the supplied metadata and predictions. The resource is intended to support further methods research; the benchmark does not establish clinical readiness or cross-centre generalisability.

item.title: A perioperative electrocardiography and photoplethysmography dataset synchronized with arterial blood gas measurements
item.description:
Dongxu Chen, Zhen Liu, Sainan Duan, Yuyang Zhang, Yu Chen, Jing Shi, Qian Lei
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08836-2
Abstract We describe a prospective multicenter perioperative dataset comprising wearable electrocardiography (ECG) and photoplethysmography (PPG) waveforms synchronized with intraoperative arterial blood gas (ABG) measurements. The dataset was collected at four medical centers in China and includes 1033 patients undergoing surgery under general anesthesia. It contains demographic and clinical characteristics, surgery- and anesthesia-related variables, serial ABG results, vital signs recorded at the time of blood sampling, medication records, and waveform files. In total, the resource includes 3313 ABG measurements and 2841 ECG/PPG waveform segments temporally aligned to blood sampling events, with most segments spanning approximately 10 minutes around sampling. Data were collected prospectively using a unified wearable acquisition system and were processed using standardized deidentification, temporal alignment, and quality-control procedures. This dataset may support research in signal processing, multimodal integration, digital biomarker discovery, non-invasive estimation of biochemical variables, and perioperative monitoring.

item.title: A 2012–2024 energy-carbon input-output dataset with new power-system detail and integrated energy-flow accounts for China
item.description:
Yan Xia, Yifan Sun, Ziyan Yang, Su Zhang, Hongqi Chen, Huijuan Wang
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08803-x
Abstract China’s energy transition is reshaping the power system and energy flows across production, transformation and consumption. Yet existing input-output data rarely distinguish storage activities within the new power system while maintaining linked accounts across these stages. Here, we present an energy-carbon input-output dataset for China covering 2012–2024. The benchmark tables for 2012, 2017 and 2023 contain 167, 177 and 235 sectors, respectively, including 35 energy subsectors. They distinguish power-generation technologies, transmission and distribution, pumped-hydro storage, generation-, grid- and user-side storage, and fossil energy extraction, processing and supply. The dataset links monetary input-output flows to integrated energy-flow accounts for 43 energy products across production, transformation and consumption, and to stage-specific CO 2 emissions accounts. Machine-learning-based annual extension yields a harmonised 177-sector series for 2012–2024. The dataset supports analyses of new power-system development, storage deployment and changes in the generation mix, as well as economy-wide energy-flow tracing and climate policy assessment.

item.title: Standardised multi-sensor geolocator data for bird migration ecology
item.description:
Raphaël Nussbaumer, Peter Adamík, Fraser Bell, Than Boves, Martins Briedis, Malcolm D. Burgess, Violeta Caballero-Lopez, Pablo Capilla-Lasheras, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08873-x
Abstract Multi-sensor geolocators using pressure-based geolocation are becoming increasingly widespread, generating a rapidly growing volume of movement data for birds, covering multiple species, geographic regions, and years. However, differences in data formats, metadata conventions, device types and manufacturers, as well as analysis workflows, currently limit data reuse and cross-study synthesis. Here, we present the GeoLocator Data Package (DP), a standardized framework to publish, curate and combine multi-sensor geolocator data within and across projects. The framework provides a unified and reproducible analysis workflow that enables individual studies using pressure-based geolocators to publish project-specific data packages following a shared structure. These packages can then be aggregated into a single dataset while preserving provenance and attribution. The framework builds on established pressure-based geolocation methods and supports consistent generation of biologically interpretable movement trajectories from multi-sensor data. By following FAIR data principles with documented tools for contributors and users, the GeoLocator DP facilitates reuse of geolocator data for comparative and macro-ecological studies of bird movement.

item.title: A global collection of wind direction-weighted topographic exposure indices (TOPEX) and topographic position indices (TPI) for non-polar land areas
item.description:
Christopher Jung, Kerstin Stahl, Dirk Schindler
Scientific Data, vol. 13, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08788-7
Abstract Topographic derivatives are widely used in applied geosciences, yet most metrics describe terrain geometry without capturing directional terrain–atmosphere interactions. We present GloTopIx, a global 250 m × 250 m data collection including anisotropic, wind direction-frequency-weighted topographic exposure ( TOPEX ) and topographic position ( TPI ) indices, together with unweighted base products derived from a harmonized digital elevation model and ERA5-derived wind climatology for 1996–2025. For each grid cell, TOPEX and TPI were computed in eight directions at four search distances (1, 5, 10, and 25 km) to capture multiscale terrain structure. The weighted variants incorporate ERA5 wind direction frequencies at 10 and 100 m, as well as 10 m frequencies under extreme wind conditions. The collection comprises 32 product variants for each of 11 non-polar regional units. Potential applications include meteorological downscaling, geomorphological landform analysis, ecological and forestry studies, hydrological and soil-moisture modeling, fire-risk assessment, and wind turbine siting. Station-based empirical assessment was restricted to Germany. Users should therefore assess the region-specific terrain–climate relationships before applying them in other regions.
